meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'oasis', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: This is an oasis of French cuisine.

examples.text: Наш ресторан — это настоящий оазис французской кухни.
examples.trans: Our restaurant is a true oasis of French cuisine.

examples.text: Тихий летний дворик стал уютным оазисом в центре Москвы.
examples.trans: The quiet summer courtyard became a cozy oasis in the center of Moscow.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('French').

examples.trans: And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'enclave', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is a true bastion of quality.

examples.text: Шеф создал здесь маленький анклав высокой кухни.
examples.trans: The chef created a small enclave of haute cuisine here.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'quality' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There won't be any quality anyway.

examples.text: Товарищ майор, тут всё очень плохо слышно. Качества всё равно не будет.
examples.trans: Comrade Major, you can barely hear anything here. There won't be any quality anyway.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.
Secondary conversational sense ('what a lot of!') (in exclamations) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
colloquial plural силы = engine horsepower
colloquial plural силы = engine horsepower

examples.trans: How much power does this car have?

examples.text: Да, по-моему, здорово! Сколько сил в этой машине?
examples.trans: Yes, I think it's great! How much power does this car have?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('invested').

examples.trans: So much effort went into this place.

examples.text: Сколько сил и труда вложено в этот ресторан.
examples.trans: So much effort and labor has been invested in this restaurant.

examples.text: Все вложенные деньги обязательно вернутся через год.
examples.trans: All the invested money will definitely return in a year.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'native' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
родной брат = full brother; родной город = hometown

examples.text: Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: Well then, my dear friend, to you!

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска! Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk! Well then, my dear friend, to you!

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'child'.

examples.trans: A waiter is like my own child.

examples.text: Каждый официант в зале для меня как родной ребёнок.
examples.trans: Every waiter in the dining room is like my own child to me.

examples.text: Для маленького ребёнка мы приготовили тёплое картофельное пюре.
examples.trans: For the young child we prepared warm mashed potatoes.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('hi') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, strictly speaking, as a matter of fact
meanings.note: softens a correction or adds a second thought

examples.text: А вообще-то я ещё не решил.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'new girl', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Познакомьтесь, это наша новенькая официантка в зале.
examples.trans: Meet her, this is our new waitress in the dining room.

examples.text: Новенькая быстро выучила всё меню нашего ресторана.
examples.trans: The new girl quickly learned the entire menu of our restaurant.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'probably'.

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: 'пойдём' / 'пойдёмте'; colloquially also 'пошли'

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'next'.
Secondary conversational sense ('next, go on') (in a list or a story) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'coffee', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'art director', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: I am the art director of the restaurant.
Vika works as the restaurant art director.
This is Viktoria Sergeyevna, our art director.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'meeting' in conversational and formal Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('date (romantic)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
